title: Events platform example

CTX.name: Accounts & organisers
CTX.desc: People who sign in, organisations that host events, and their team memberships.

CTX.name: Events
CTX.desc: Reusable event listings, their dated occurrences, and discovery categories.

CTX.name: Venues
CTX.desc: Physical venues and their bookable rooms or spaces.

CTX.name: Programme
CTX.desc: The sessions and speakers within an event occurrence.

CTX.name: Ticketing
CTX.desc: Ticket products, capacity, sales windows, and temporary checkout reservations.

CTX.name: Sales & payments
CTX.desc: Purchases, price snapshots, discounts, payment attempts, and partial refunds.

CTX.name: Attendance
CTX.desc: Ticket holders, issued tickets, transfers, admission records, and waiting lists.

CTX.name: Communications
CTX.desc: Event announcements and a record of each email delivery.

ENT.desc: A sign-in account. A buyer, organiser team member, or attendee may use the same account. Authentication secrets belong in a separate identity system.

f.note: Unique after trimming and case-insensitive comparison.

ENT.desc: An organisation or individual that owns event listings and receives their sales proceeds.
checks: At least one active OrganizerMember has the owner role.
An active owner membership refers to an active account. Removing or suspending the last active owner is prohibited.

ENT.desc: Connects an account to an organiser team and records its role. One account can belong to several organisers.
checks: Removed memberships have removed_at; active and suspended memberships do not. Rejoining reactivates the existing membership.

ENT.desc: A reusable discovery category, such as music or workshops. This is a controlled classification, not an event owner.
The public listing and shared description of an event. Each dated run is an EventOccurrence; recurring events reuse this listing.
An explicit link that allows an event to appear in multiple categories without duplicating event or category data.
One dated run of an event. It has its own time, location, capacity, programme, ticket products, and waiting list.

f.note: IANA time-zone name used to display the UTC timestamps.
Maximum number of issued valid tickets plus active, unexpired reserved places.

checks: ends_at > starts_at; capacity >= 0.
At least one of venue_space_id and online_url is present; both may be set for a hybrid event.
For a physical occurrence, capacity <= its venue space capacity.
time_zone is an IANA time-zone identifier. Timestamps are absolute UTC instants; ambiguous or nonexistent local input times are resolved before storage.
Overlapping scheduled physical occurrences cannot book the same venue space; cancelled occurrences do not reserve a space.

ENT.desc: A physical location that can contain one or more event spaces. The address is a value object, not a separate business entity.

f.note: A structured address; postal codes are optional because some countries do not use them.

ENT.desc: A room, hall, stage, or other bookable space within a venue. Different event occurrences can reuse the same space.
checks: capacity > 0.

ENT.desc: A talk, performance, workshop, or other scheduled activity within one occurrence. Sessions do not sell separate tickets in this example.
checks: starts_at < ends_at; the session is within its occurrence time range.
When venue_space_id is set, it belongs to the occurrence venue.
A physical session uses a space in the occurrence venue; an online-only occurrence has no physical session space. Sessions sharing a space cannot overlap.

ENT.desc: A reusable public speaker or performer profile. Being a speaker does not require having a sign-in account.
Connects speakers to sessions. A session can have several speakers, and a speaker can appear in several sessions.

f.note: For example host, speaker, or performer.

checks: display_order >= 0.

ENT.desc: A sellable ticket product for one occurrence, such as general admission or a concession. Capacity and sales windows belong to this product.
checks: capacity >= 0; max_per_order > 0.
sales_start_at < sales_end_at <= occurrence.starts_at.
Issued non-voided tickets plus active, unexpired reservations do not exceed ticket-type capacity or occurrence capacity.
Sales require a published event and a scheduled occurrence; no reservation is created outside the sales window. Capacity changes cannot reduce limits below existing admissions and live holds.

ENT.desc: A temporary quantity hold for one order item. The item identifies the order, ticket type and occurrence. Repeated checkout attempts retain separate reservation history; at most one hold is active per item.
checks: quantity > 0; expires_at > created_at.
An active or converted reservation matches its order item quantity and does not exceed ticket_type.max_per_order.
An active reservation consumes capacity only while unexpired and its order is pending. A confirmed order has no active reservations.
Conversion and ticket issuance are atomic: the hold is released as exactly quantity tickets are issued. Expiry, release and conversion retain the reservation record.

ENT.desc: An organiser-owned discount, optionally restricted to one event. Its terms are copied into order-item price snapshots at purchase time.

f.note: Three-letter currency code; required for a fixed-amount discount.

checks: valid_from < valid_until; value > 0; max_redemptions is absent or > 0.
Percentage discounts have value <= 100 and no currency; fixed-amount discounts require a currency.
A restricted event belongs to the same organiser; a code applies only to eligible orders.

Percentage and fixed discounts are rounded deterministically to currency minor units and cannot make an eligible item total negative. A redemption hold is a pending eligible order with active, unexpired ticket reservations; these holds and confirmed orders count toward max_redemptions.

ENT.desc: One checkout with a single organiser and currency. The buyer may purchase tickets for several attendees; guest checkout does not require an account.

f.note: Contact snapshot retained with the purchase.

checks: All order items belong to this organiser and use the order currency.
total.amount equals the sum of order-item totals.
A confirmed order has at least one item. A paid order has exactly one successful applied payment equal to its total; free orders have no applied payment. Split payments are outside this example.
A discount is redeemed once per confirmed order; confirmed redemptions do not exceed its limit.
Pending orders may have no items. Confirmed orders have confirmed_at and immutable item quantities and price snapshots; cancellation does not delete financial history.

ENT.desc: A purchased quantity of one ticket type. Price, discount, and tax are immutable snapshots; later ticket-price changes do not change this purchase.
checks: quantity > 0 and quantity <= ticket_type.max_per_order.
All money values use the order currency; discount <= quantity * unit_price.
total.amount = quantity * unit_price.amount - discount.amount + tax.amount.
A confirmed order item issues exactly quantity tickets; voided tickets remain in its history.
For a confirmed order, the issued tickets paid_amount values sum exactly to total.amount; nonrefundable or fee-only products are outside this model.

ENT.desc: One payment attempt against an order. Failed attempts are retained and a later attempt has a separate identity. No card numbers or payment secrets are stored.

f.note: Original provider status, retained separately from the normalised domain state.
Provider failure or reconciliation reason; no payment secrets.
True only for the single successful capture used to confirm this order. It remains true after ticket-return refunds; late or duplicate captures stay unapplied.

checks: amount.amount > 0 and uses the order currency.
paid_at is present for succeeded payments. Captures exceeding the unpaid order balance are retained and receive unapplied_payment refunds; provider facts are never discarded.
Payment success, order confirmation, reservation conversion and ticket issuance are idempotent and atomic; a late success after expiry requires available capacity or an explicit compensating refund.
Unapplied-payment refunds compensate unapplied captures without issuing tickets; ticket-return refunds preserve the original applied payment and purchase history.

is_applied is true only for a succeeded capture equal to the order total that confirmed the order; at most one payment is applied per order. Other successful captures remain unapplied and are compensated in full.

ENT.desc: One full or partial return of a successful payment. The affected order-item quantities are recorded in RefundItem.

f.note: A ticket return or compensation for an unexpected payment capture.
Original provider status, retained separately from the normalised domain state.
Provider failure or reconciliation reason; no payment secrets.

checks: The payment succeeded; the refund uses its currency and has a positive amount.

A ticket_return has at least one RefundItem and amount equals their amount sum. A unapplied_payment has no RefundItems and returns an unapplied capture from a cancelled, expired or excess-paid checkout.
Requested plus pending plus succeeded refunds do not exceed the payment amount; succeeded refunds have refunded_at.
Refund submission, exclusive ticket allocation, success or failure, and capacity release are applied transactionally and idempotently.
A ticket_return references the order applied payment. An unapplied_payment refund references a payment with is_applied false; the full capture is compensated without ticket allocations.

ENT.desc: Allocates a refund to a quantity from one original order item, making partial ticket refunds explicit.
checks: quantity > 0; amount.amount > 0; the order item belongs to the refunded payment order.
quantity equals the number of RefundTicket allocations; amount equals their tickets paid_amount sum in the order currency.
Requested, pending and succeeded allocations never refund a ticket twice and do not exceed the original order-item total.
This example refunds complete unused tickets. Arbitrary goodwill or fee-only credits require a separate credit model.

ENT.desc: An immutable allocation of one refund item to one specific ticket. Failed refund attempts retain their selected tickets; later attempts use new allocations. This example refunds complete unused tickets, allowing a partial refund of an order.
uk: (ticket_id) across requested, pending and succeeded refunds
checks: The ticket belongs to the refund item order item, has a positive paid_amount, and has no CheckIn.
A ticket has at most one requested, pending or succeeded refund allocation. Failed or cancelled allocations remain historical and do not prevent a new attempt.
A succeeded allocation refunds exactly the ticket paid_amount in the same currency and voids the ticket.

ENT.desc: A person who can hold tickets or join a waiting list. The attendee may differ from the buyer and may optionally link to a sign-in account.
One issued admission for one person, derived from its order item and ticket type. It may be unassigned until claimed; the buyer is not automatically the attendee.

f.note: Opaque, unique admission identifier; no personal data is embedded.
Immutable per-ticket allocation of the order-item total, including discount and tax.

checks: The order was confirmed when the ticket was issued; its order item identifies the occurrence and ticket type.
paid_amount uses the order currency; the issued tickets of one order item sum exactly to its total, using a deterministic minor-unit allocation.
checked_in is equivalent to having a CheckIn record. A checked-in ticket cannot be refunded or voided in this example.
A ticket with a requested or pending refund allocation has status refund_pending and cannot be admitted or transferred. Failed or cancelled allocations release this hold.
A succeeded refund allocation requires status voided. Other cancellations may also void unused tickets; all ticket records are retained.

A failed or cancelled refund attempt releases refund_pending holds on otherwise valid tickets. A ticket already voided after an earlier refund outcome remains voided; financial retry does not silently restore admission.

ENT.desc: An invitation to hand an unused ticket to someone else. Email and sender identity are retained even before the recipient claims the ticket.
checks: At most one pending transfer per ticket; the ticket is valid, has no CheckIn, and has no active refund allocation.
The initiating account was authorised by the buyer or current holder when the transfer was created. Sending a transfer requires a sign-in account; receiving one does not.
expires_at > created_at; acceptance occurs before expiry. An accepted transfer has to_attendee_id and accepted_at and atomically assigns the ticket to that attendee.
from_attendee_id is a snapshot of the holder at creation. A pending transfer can succeed only if the holder is unchanged; sender and recipient must differ.

ENT.desc: The admission record for one ticket. A unique ticket reference prevents a second admission; optional gate information records where it happened.
checks: The ticket is assigned to an attendee, is valid immediately before admission, and has no active refund allocation.
The staff account was an active member of the occurrence organiser team at checked_in_at. Later membership removal does not invalidate this history.
Creating CheckIn and changing the ticket to checked_in are one atomic operation; the unique ticket reference makes admission idempotent.

ENT.desc: A request for places at a sold-out occurrence, optionally for a specific ticket type. Offers can link to a temporary reservation during checkout.
uk: (occurrence_id, attendee_id) while status is waiting or offered
checks: quantity > 0; a selected ticket type belongs to the same occurrence.
An offered entry has offered_at < offer_expires_at; any linked reservation matches the occurrence and quantity.
A converted entry points to a converted reservation.
A linked reservation identifies an order item for the same occurrence and selected ticket type, and quantity matches. An offer is converted only after that order is confirmed.

ENT.desc: An organiser message for an event, such as a programme update. Drafts become published announcements, with a separate delivery record for each recipient.
checks: A published announcement has published_at.

ENT.desc: One email delivery of a published announcement to an attendee. The destination address is a snapshot, and failures remain visible for retry.
checks: The announcement is published; attempt_count >= 0; sent deliveries have sent_at.
The attendee has a ticket for an occurrence of the announcement event. Retries update this delivery record; sent_at is present exactly when status is sent.

ENUMNOTES.AccountStatus: Whether an account can use the service.
ENUMNOTES.OrganizerRole: Access role within one organiser team.
ENUMNOTES.EventStatus: Publication state of the shared event listing.
ENUMNOTES.OccurrenceStatus: State of one dated run, independently of other runs.
ENUMNOTES.ReservationStatus: Whether a checkout hold still consumes ticket capacity.
ENUMNOTES.DiscountKind: Interpretation of the discount value and optional currency.
ENUMNOTES.OrderStatus: State of one checkout; confirmed orders retain their financial history.
ENUMNOTES.TicketStatus: Admission validity of one issued ticket.
ENUMNOTES.TransferStatus: Progress of an invitation to reassign a ticket.
ENUMNOTES.WaitlistStatus: Progress from waiting for availability through an offer to purchase.
ENUMNOTES.AnnouncementStatus: Whether an event message is ready for recipients.
ENUMNOTES.DeliveryStatus: Outcome of sending one announcement email.
ENUMNOTES.MembershipStatus: Current membership state; removal retains the team relationship and its history.
ENUMNOTES.RefundKind: Ticket returns allocate specific unused tickets; payment reversals return unapplied captures without pretending tickets were issued.

f.note: Supported uppercase ISO 4217 currency code; supported currencies and minor units are configured by the implementing service.

TYPES.d: A nonnegative exact decimal amount paired with an ISO 4217 currency code. Monetary settlement values use the currency minor-unit precision and an explicit deterministic rounding policy. Different currencies cannot be added.
A physical address stored as one value object on a venue.

PRIMS: An absolute timestamp stored in UTC.
